rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes a YSZ interlayer diffusion barrier, while the paper uses compositional alloying of a refractory high-entropy alloy coating with Al. These are fundamentally different kinds of interventions (a separate interlayer vs. alloying within the coating), so the intervention type does not match.
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis mentions subcritical-water operation and high-temperature steam per standard protocols, while the paper uses isothermal oxidation in flowing steam at 1000 °C for 60 min and 1100 °C for 30 min. Both involve high-temperature steam, but the hypothesis lacks the paper's specific temperature, time, and steam flow conditions.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes a physical diffusion barrier (YSZ) to suppress Cr–Zr interdiffusion, whereas the paper's mechanism relies on the formation of a protective Al2O3-TiO2-Cr2O3 composite oxide layer that suppresses oxygen diffusion and preserves adhesion. These are different classes of mechanism (diffusion barrier vs. protective oxide formation).
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts reduced Cr–Zr interdiffusion and preserved protective properties, while the paper predicts and measures minimized oxidation rate and oxygen penetration with an optimal Al content. Both aim for improved protection, but the specific property (interdiffusion vs. oxidation resistance) and the nature of the comparison differ.
